planting.note: Root stem cuttings in barely damp cactus mix and keep in bright, filtered light rather than direct sun, since this Brazilian forest epiphyte grows naturally tucked into tree bark crevices in dappled shade.

directions: Pot in a chunky, fast-draining epiphytic mix and grow in a hanging basket where the distinctive four-angled, cross-sectioned stems can cascade freely. Water when the mix approaches dryness and never let the roots sit wet, mimicking the humid-but-airy conditions of its native tree-canopy habitat. Small cream to pale pink flowers appear along the stem ridges in spring, followed by translucent pink berries. Keep out of direct sun, which scorches the thin stem segments; an east window or shaded porch suits it well.
